值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析媒體如何透過「貼標籤」與簡化機制，將社會焦慮轉嫁至弱勢族群並引發對立。
  • 結合高夫曼、吉爾、傅柯、薩伊德與霍爾等多位大師的社會學與傳播理論，提供扎實的批判性思考架構。
  • 透過台灣空服員罷工與原住民爭取權益等真實案例，揭露主流媒體如何以「視覺消費」與「刻板印象」抹煞抗爭者的真實話語權。

摘要

媒體標籤與社會污名化機制

作者指出，現代媒體為迎合大眾有限的注意力，慣用「化繁為簡」的標題將特定群體與社會問題劃上等號。這種簡化對主流群體而言是便捷摘要，對邊緣弱勢族群卻是長期的制度化傷害。作者引用社會學家高夫曼（Erving Goffman）的理論，說明污名（Stigma）並非個人內在缺陷，而是一種社會關係，源自於大眾預期的「虛擬社會身分」與「真實社會身分」產生落差。媒體透過身體污名、性格污名與族群污名，利用「全面性缺陷」的心理機制將少數個案放大為群體標籤，藉由製造道德恐慌（Moral Panic）將邊緣族群塑造成社會焦慮的代罪羔羊。

後女性主義與抗爭訴求的視覺消費化

作者以台灣空服員罷工為例，揭示媒體如何透過鏡頭轉移焦點來消解嚴肅議題。原本抗議過勞排班與爭取勞動權益的集體行動，在媒體鏡頭下卻聚焦於女性外貌與身材，被包裝成「最美罷工風景」。作者引述學者吉爾（Rosalind Gill）的後女性主義觀點以及傅柯（Michel Foucault）的權力理論，指出媒體常將女性包裝為「自主追求美麗的主體」，實質上是將被凝視的權力結構內化為審美規訓。當勞動訴求被置換為長腿與顏值，一場體制抗爭便被徹底降格為供大眾娛樂的視覺消費秀。

他者化與刻板印象的四重齒輪

作者進一步探討原住民族群在媒體報導中的失語困境。當原住民青年身著現代服裝爭取土地正義與母語權益時，媒體往往將其套上傳統服飾並冠上「勇士」稱號，抹煞其當代處境。作者結合薩伊德（Edward Said）的他者化（Othering）概念與霍爾（Stuart Hall）的刻板印象理論，拆解媒體運作的四重齒輪：化約（Reduction）、本質化（Essentialization）、自然化（Naturalization）與固著（Fixation）。主流媒體將多元豐富的文化深度簡化為迪士尼式的「公主」與「勇士」，用看似讚美的標籤掩飾真實壓迫，使大眾忽視原住民族群在現實社會中所面臨的真正困境。

================================================

Hello! Everyone! This is A-Niu. Today let us talk about media "labeling" You may ask, is this important. Of course it is important. because this label. very easily causes social antagonism. When you watch the news. you must have seen similar headlines. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "Most beautiful striking flight attendant sits in under the blazing sun" "Young people are poor only because they do not work hard" Every news headline. is like a simple equation. Some person. equals some kind of social problem. You scroll your phone very fast. almost never stopping to think. Without your knowing it. inside your head. labels have already been stuck on one after another. After you turn off your phone. have these labels disappeared. But have you ever thought. why they headline it this way. Because every day too many things happen in the world. and our brain's attention is too weak. So the media choose. to "simplify the complex" But the problem is this simplifying of the complex. for the mainstream group. is a thoughtful summary cheat sheet. but for marginal disadvantaged groups. it is a slow torture. A corporate CEO. if simplified or misunderstood by the news. still has a huge PR. and lawyer team to help him clarify. But a migrant worker. a mental illness patient. when he is simplified into a headline by the news. that label often follows him for a lifetime. What is more frightening. is that once a label has been stuck on long enough. society becomes used to it as normal. This is what in academia is called. "institutionalization" and "normalization" So today let us talk about "labels" Two thousand years ago. if you were a slave or traitor. a mark would be branded on your skin. In Greek it is called stigma. that is, "stigmatization" This mark is very crude. With just one glance. everyone automatically stays 3 meters away from you. Now we no longer brand the skin. but switch to headlining. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "The deadly menace of the shut-in geek" The label is stamped onto the screen. and the effect is exactly the same. Sociology master Goffman. laid bare one thing. Stigma is not "something on your body" but a kind of "social relationship" Put simply. it is not that you are inherently problematic. but that society collectively decides. that some attribute of yours should be devalued. When we look at people we usually have two scripts. One is "virtual social identity" that is, we look at your appearance. and blindly guess in our heads. what kind of person you "should" be. The other is "actual social identity" that is, what kind of person. you "actually" are. When these two cannot connect. and happen to step on society's prejudice pain point. the label gets stuck on. Brother Goffman divides stigma into three major categories. which everyone can use to compare against today's news. The first category is bodily stigma. like disability or appearance differences. The media often portray them as. weaklings who can only be given charity. The second category is character stigma. like mental illness. unemployment or addiction. Complex social-institutional problems. are often simplified by the media into. "he just does not work hard himself" The third category is ethnic stigma. This is most often carried along by bloodline. The media often take a specific ethnic group. and directly equate it with specific criminals.

This labeling routine's. most powerful weapon is called "generalized flaw" The meaning is. that as long as one sees a black dot on you. the brain will automatically paint the whole thing black. When seeing "fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" what everyone thinks is not. "this 'one' person committed a crime" but they equate "all migrant workers" with "public order blind spots" This is actually collective anxiety grabbing a scapegoat. In communication studies it is called "moral panic" When everyone's days are hard. and they have no sense of security about the future. the media need only throw out a disadvantaged group. and the public's fury and unease. immediately have an outlet for venting. Discrimination is legalized all the way from the everyday. into stricter policies of exclusion. In the past the ancient Greek iron brand. could only scorch one person at a time. Modern media's steel seal. directly brands an entire group of people. directly making people too lazy to think. The previous segment talked about how media use labels. to demonize people. This segment let us look at a real example. In the past. Taiwan's flight attendants. once organized a strike. They sat in under the blazing sun. holding banners in their hands. protesting overwork scheduling. unreasonable wages. and working hours they could barely endure. At this point the media came. By rights their mission. is to convey the demands to the public. But this camera. was not aimed at the protest banners. but instead lingered on the calves. The next day's headline. "The most beautiful strike scenery" "Good-looking flight attendants sit in under the blazing sun" So in this strike. what did the audience finally see. Why is it that whenever women walk into the public sphere. the media's camera always "accidentally" tilts from their demands. onto their bodies. British scholar Gill. in "Gender and the Media" pointed out a very contradictory phenomenon. called "postfeminism" On one hand. the media shout "the rise of girl power" every day. But on the other hand. in the same channel. they sell body anxiety. Advertisements and reports that take women's figures. as a selling point. have never been in short supply. Gill points out. that the media play a very clever word game. In the past they treated women. as "objects to be looked at" Now they package women. as "subjects who actively want to become pretty" It sounds as if it is more progressive. but actually it is worse. because the power structure of "being stared at" has already been internalized into women's minds. Dieting. photo-editing. crazy fitness training. under the media's packaging. all become "pampering yourself" "being yourself" So a woman confidently showing off her figure. autonomously deciding how to dress up. is this not freedom. French thinker Foucault, Gill. their rebuttal is very sharp. The difference in it lies in. that the "list of autonomous options" you tick. exactly who wrote it. When the media take "appearance" as the unwritten rule of public exposure. where if you are not pretty no one pays you attention. you think you are freely choosing. but actually you are just obeying a set of. invisible rules. Looking back at the flight attendant strike (slip of the tongue). This was originally a labor-management. dispute concerning overwork scheduling. and high-pressure management. What it needed was society's.

rational dialogue about labor rights. As a result. the media did not film the data on the negotiation table. but specially filmed the profile of flight attendants wiping sweat. The headlines were uniformly. "The most beautiful strike scenery" A political protest against the system. was rewritten into one that lets everyone. feast their eyes on ice cream. a "visual consumption show" This camera that deliberately slides downward. is this label. machine's second gear. It does not directly tell you to shut up. It tells you to smile more sweetly. When your labor demands, in the news,. are swapped out for your waistline and your face. no matter how loud you shout. what more people pay attention to is instead. those enviable long legs. Now let us change direction. and aim the camera at an indigenous youth. This time the media did not tell him to shut up. but helped him change into a set of "costume" An Amis youth. wearing a modern shirt. at a press conference talking about land justice. the loss of traditional territory and the rupture of the mother tongue. these are all his contemporary situation. As a result the next day's news footage. showed indigenous costumes from who knows where. plus a big knife. The subtitle showed "Amis warrior" At that point who still remembers what demands he stated. Why is it that when mainstream society. is "praising" a minority group. they instead lose the right to speak. In postcolonial theory master. Said's "Orientalism" there is a concept called "othering" Put simply. the mainstream group with power. is not "describing" the disadvantaged. but "inventing" the disadvantaged. through the media painting the other side as. a backward. mysterious. exotic land. emphasizing that they and oneself. are "essentially different" This way mainstream society can. justifiably go manage him. even speak on his behalf. Cultural studies giant Hall. takes "stereotype" and dismantles it into four gears. The first is reduction. reducing a person's personality and background. down to only a few characteristics. Next is. essentialization. saying these few characteristics. are what this ethnic group. "innately carries in its DNA" Then. naturalization. taking artificially imposed categorization. and packaging it as "nature's original law" Finally fixation. making this flattened image jammed dead. forever not allowed to change. When these four gears turn to the end. they cut the world into two halves. On one side is "normal us" On the other side is. "abnormal them, full of peculiar exotic flavor" This machine, in Taiwan,. exactly how does it operate. The most typical. is the media's coverage of indigenous peoples. Actually each indigenous. people's institutions differ greatly. Some are matrilineal societies. some have strict class systems. and some have egalitarian elder councils. But in mainstream media. this depth and diversity. all disappear. Replacing them is a set of. Disney-cartoon-style words. "princess" "warrior" "chieftain" You may think. "princess" and "warrior" does this not sound like praise. what is wrong with this.

This is actually what Hall called. "naturalization"'s most vicious aspect. When the media use these "beautiful labels" to cover up all the real-world plight. the true problem can no longer be spoken. When the public becomes used to it. that indigenous people should, at the harvest festival,. sing and dance. innately passionate and humorous. what they, in reality,. face in employment discrimination. land rights being encroached upon. these get silenced by the singing and dancing. The Amis youth who was edited into festival footage. is not the TV station's error. but this label. machine's third gear. When mainstream society. insists on making you put on the "warrior" costume. before it is willing to give you the camera. you will find that this kind of. applause-carrying praise. is sometimes a gentler. and harder-to-remove hush money. So when the object this machine films. is not some ethnic group. but a poor person drifting on the streets. what kind of camera will it use. to make you believe. "his being poor is his own fault" You may have seen this kind of footage. a cramped little studio apartment. clothes scattered all over the floor. the kitchen full of grease. a single mother crouching in the corner. with a crying child beside her. The narration's tone is pressed very low. "She has no skill. the child's formula money. to this day still has no source" In just twenty seconds. at the moment you finish watching. a trace of sympathy may first rise in your heart. But perhaps there will be another voice. "Why does she not find a job. why does she not work a bit harder" This thinking process from "sympathy" turning toward "condemnation" is not because you are cold-blooded. but because this camera. chose a specific shot for you. American communication scholar Iyengar. did over a hundred experiments. and reached a conclusion. The way the media tell stories. is not only reporting news. but even more "assigning responsibility" He takes the media's narrative frame. and cuts it into two kinds of shots. One is the episodic frame. pushing the camera infinitely close. staring dead at some. "individual" or specific event. The other is the thematic frame. pulling the camera far away. to present, behind the event,. its "environment" and structural data. Brother Iyengar's experiment discovered. a major loophole in human nature. When the audience watches for a whole week straight. "telephoto lens" individual-case reporting. the brain will instinctively attribute poverty. crime or unemployment. all to. "the person himself being lazy. not working hard enough" Conversely. only when the audience sees. "wide-angle lens" thematic reporting. will they begin to reflect on the labor market. housing policy. and the social safety net, these institutional problems. The same social problem. with just a change of shot. the object of blame changes along with it. So why do today's media. so favor the telephoto lens. The reason is very realistic. The story is engaging. the cost is low. the emotional tension is strong. Filming an individual case's tears. takes only 20 seconds to hand in the job. But if one is to pull the camera far. and film clearly the labor market's structure. the media must spend 3 months. interviewing dozens of experts.

retrieving countless official documents. reports. In the torrent of instant news. the cost incentives of economy and time. overwhelm everything. Some people may speak up for the media. using individual-case stories to arouse sympathy. launch donation drives. making abstract issues have warmth. is this not a good thing. The key to the problem. has never been "having" individual cases. but that the media have "only" individual cases. When among 100 news items discussing poverty. 99 are all using the telephoto lens to push close. close-up on the person's misery. the audience's brain will be left with only. "this is all his personal problem" this standard answer. Political philosopher Fraser. criticizes this phenomenon very sharply. Mainstream media are most skilled at. taking institutional problems belonging to the public sphere. and "individualizing and familializing" them. The media package the problem as a family tragedy. quietly driving it off the negotiation table of debate. In sociology this. is the most typical "blaming the victim" Returning to that single mother. if today the media were willing to pull the camera far. switch to wide-angle, what would we see. We would see the closed-down factory. the rent risen to the ceiling. the severely insufficient public childcare. We would even see. the problem of the welfare-status review system. how, in reality, it takes countless. people on the edge of absolute poverty. and legally blocks them outside the door of social assistance. But these key institutional problems. the telephoto lens cannot fit in even one frame. So the distance of the camera. finally decides. society's conscience and resources. where they will finally be placed. Let us take a look. at when the media take all the gears. and aim them simultaneously at the same person. what will happen. On March 28, 2016. in Neihu a 4-year-old little girl. was killed by a stranger before her mother's eyes. From the incident to that evening. you turned on the TV. scrolled open your phone. and the headlines were uniformly. "mentally ill suspect" followed by "time bomb" "weirdo who calls himself Emperor Yao" "neighbors all thought he was strange" "loved playing violent video games" These words came overwhelmingly. In less than 24 hours. the puzzle in everyone's head. was pieced together. When "mentally ill suspect" these words fell down. did the fear in your heart. suddenly get settled down. Why, while everyone is still in shock,. are the media in such a hurry. to stuff the words "mental illness" into everyone's heads. Because this label. is actually society's collective. anxiety's fast painkiller. American scholar Wahl. in "Media Madness" points out. that the media always disproportionately. tie mental illness. violence. and villains together. And they dislike using medical terms. using in large quantities "lunatic" "psycho," this kind of slang. This is not only disrespectful. This is saving the audience the effort of "thinking" compressing complex medical and social problems. into an instantly understood terror symbol. But what is truly heartbreaking. are those details deleted by the headline. Like the killer, in 2010 and 2014,. had already shown behavior of attacking neighbors. and was also diagnosed with schizophrenia. That is to say. before the tragedy happened. our social safety net.

had already failed to catch him for a full 6 years. But this 6 years of "failure to catch" in that day's headlines. you cannot see a single word. The media do not want to explain. how the tragedy happened. It only wants to tell you "the killer is a monster" because exploring the causes behind it is too tiring. too complex. too sleep-depriving. So the media thoughtfully skip over it for you. Three years later, in July 2019,. Chiayi railway police officer Lee Cheng-han. was stabbed to death in the line of duty. The suspect likewise had schizophrenia. and likewise had long had medical records. likewise had discontinued medication. The words the media used. the rhythm. the footage. were almost exactly the same as three years before. The script did not change. only the actor was swapped. When the same play is staged repeatedly. this is no longer an individual event. but a stably operating structure. Since this medicine treats the symptom not the root. why does everyone still swallow it. Because every time a major random crime. the early morning the day after it erupts. while you eat breakfast. watching on the TV. a pundit angrily slam the table and shout. "this kind of lunatic should all be locked up" At this moment in your heart. a strange sense of relief will rise. because in that instant. between "the killer" and "you" a line is drawn. He is abnormal. and you are normal. This is not the solidness brought by truth. but a psychological defense line the media built for you. When extreme violence occurs in society. the answer we least want to hear. is instead that the killer. is actually an ordinary person. because this answer is too heavy. If we admit. that the killer is not some alien. but a person just like us. living under a high-pressure society. only that in isolation. failed to be caught by the system. with no way to retreat, he snapped. behind it actually represents. that crime is not walled off outside. but lurks in every overworked family. every laid-off middle-aged man. every living room before someone is caught. If we accept this truth. all Taiwan tonight, no one could sleep. So the media's machine starts at full speed. Hall's "division" gear begins to turn. classifying the suspect as "the abnormal other" confirming us as "safe normal people" Iyengar's "telephoto lens" is also pushed to the very front. The camera aims at that abnormal brain. while the world outside the wide-angle lens. the overworked labor environment. the safety net full of holes. the long-insufficient mental-health resources. are all locked into darkness. In Taiwanese society every time after a case. our real reaction. is the best evidence. On social media it is forever. "lock up the lunatics" "compulsory treatment cannot be delayed" "mental illness equals a death-exemption gold medal" "death penalty the only option" The core of these slogans. is all not asking why. they went long uncaught. but "how to cut them out" Communication scholar Gerbner. puts it very heavily. This kind of attribution only helps us. escape collective responsibility. When you shout to lock them up. sentence them to death. your anxiety is relieved. but the core that could truly solve the problem. is also let go with your own hands. But this wall is not un-topplable. In that year's incident.

the person most entitled to be angry. Little Light Bulb's mother, Wang Wan-yu,. instead refused the media's. handed-over painkiller. She did not shout along. to lock up all the lunatics. but calmly asked society. to mend the holes in the safety net. She said in court. that compared to the killer being executed. she cared more about. "the next time I take my child out to the street. not needing to be on edge with worry anymore" Although some people. would, because of ideology. or differences in political stance. use the tragedy that happened to her. to make some jokes. but after years of advocacy. the "Mental Health Act" in 2022. completed a large-scale revision. This proves one thing. The wall the media blocked up for you. everyone can push open with their own hands. But the premise is. that we are willing to hear the crying outside the wall. rather than being in a hurry to swallow the painkiller. When the majority of people. still choose to swallow the painkiller. pretending the world is very safe. the ones truly silently bearing the pain. exactly who are they. Actually it is every one of us. When you lie on the sofa scrolling your phone. a sensational crime headline. a simplified poverty close-up. an indigenous youth crowned with "princess" or "warrior" At this point please stop and ask yourself. while the media label things for us. how should you press the pause button. As a modern citizen. what weapons do we have left to resist it. A-Niu feels that every one of us. has two major self-defense moves. "decoding" and "resistance" "Decoding" is learning. to see through the magic behind the news. Next time you see the news. try to dismantle in your heart. whether its camera is pushing infinitely close. or slowly pulling far. Is it focusing on personal grudges. or presenting the social context. How many times does it let some identity label. get repeatedly bombarded. On whom does it finally. blame the responsibility. These four questions. are your magnifying glass for dismantling media labels. "Resistance" is refusing to be an accomplice. When you scroll to a. report attributing poverty to "not working hard" you can choose not to like it. not to forward it. When you see a labor protest. simplified into "the most beautiful strike scenery" you can proactively refuse to watch. and turn to find independent media that earnestly report. When you see "mentally ill suspect" again beginning to occupy all the pages. you can choose to press, in the comment section,. whether that social safety net that failed to catch him. over the past few years has been mended or not. A-Niu finally leaves a question. I want to hear everyone's views. When mainstream media continue to use. "princess" "warrior" or "innately optimistic and loves to drink," these words. to consume indigenous peoples. if you hold the microphone of self-media. how would you return the right to speak to them. letting them use their own words. to tell their own contemporary stories. We welcome everyone to share your views. Our channel has always been. committed to the idea of "rebuilding the republic" hoping through civic. education and historical awareness. to awaken everyone's. appreciation for democratic values. If you enjoyed this episode. do not forget to like. subscribe. and share it with more people. You are also welcome to join our membership.

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析媒體如何透過「貼標籤」與簡化機制，將社會焦慮轉嫁至弱勢族群並引發對立。
  • 結合高夫曼、吉爾、傅柯、薩伊德與霍爾等多位大師的社會學與傳播理論，提供扎實的批判性思考架構。
  • 透過台灣空服員罷工與原住民爭取權益等真實案例，揭露主流媒體如何以「視覺消費」與「刻板印象」抹煞抗爭者的真實話語權。

摘要

媒體標籤與社會污名化機制

作者指出，現代媒體為迎合大眾有限的注意力，慣用「化繁為簡」的標題將特定群體與社會問題劃上等號。這種簡化對主流群體而言是便捷摘要，對邊緣弱勢族群卻是長期的制度化傷害。作者引用社會學家高夫曼（Erving Goffman）的理論，說明污名（Stigma）並非個人內在缺陷，而是一種社會關係，源自於大眾預期的「虛擬社會身分」與「真實社會身分」產生落差。媒體透過身體污名、性格污名與族群污名，利用「全面性缺陷」的心理機制將少數個案放大為群體標籤，藉由製造道德恐慌（Moral Panic）將邊緣族群塑造成社會焦慮的代罪羔羊。

後女性主義與抗爭訴求的視覺消費化

作者以台灣空服員罷工為例，揭示媒體如何透過鏡頭轉移焦點來消解嚴肅議題。原本抗議過勞排班與爭取勞動權益的集體行動，在媒體鏡頭下卻聚焦於女性外貌與身材，被包裝成「最美罷工風景」。作者引述學者吉爾（Rosalind Gill）的後女性主義觀點以及傅柯（Michel Foucault）的權力理論，指出媒體常將女性包裝為「自主追求美麗的主體」，實質上是將被凝視的權力結構內化為審美規訓。當勞動訴求被置換為長腿與顏值，一場體制抗爭便被徹底降格為供大眾娛樂的視覺消費秀。

他者化與刻板印象的四重齒輪

作者進一步探討原住民族群在媒體報導中的失語困境。當原住民青年身著現代服裝爭取土地正義與母語權益時，媒體往往將其套上傳統服飾並冠上「勇士」稱號，抹煞其當代處境。作者結合薩伊德（Edward Said）的他者化（Othering）概念與霍爾（Stuart Hall）的刻板印象理論，拆解媒體運作的四重齒輪：化約（Reduction）、本質化（Essentialization）、自然化（Naturalization）與固著（Fixation）。主流媒體將多元豐富的文化深度簡化為迪士尼式的「公主」與「勇士」，用看似讚美的標籤掩飾真實壓迫，使大眾忽視原住民族群在現實社會中所面臨的真正困境。

================================================

Hello! Everyone! This is A-Niu. Today let us talk about media "labeling" You may ask, is this important. Of course it is important. because this label. very easily causes social antagonism. When you watch the news. you must have seen similar headlines. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "Most beautiful striking flight attendant sits in under the blazing sun" "Young people are poor only because they do not work hard" Every news headline. is like a simple equation. Some person. equals some kind of social problem. You scroll your phone very fast. almost never stopping to think. Without your knowing it. inside your head. labels have already been stuck on one after another. After you turn off your phone. have these labels disappeared. But have you ever thought. why they headline it this way. Because every day too many things happen in the world. and our brain's attention is too weak. So the media choose. to "simplify the complex" But the problem is this simplifying of the complex. for the mainstream group. is a thoughtful summary cheat sheet. but for marginal disadvantaged groups. it is a slow torture. A corporate CEO. if simplified or misunderstood by the news. still has a huge PR. and lawyer team to help him clarify. But a migrant worker. a mental illness patient. when he is simplified into a headline by the news. that label often follows him for a lifetime. What is more frightening. is that once a label has been stuck on long enough. society becomes used to it as normal. This is what in academia is called. "institutionalization" and "normalization" So today let us talk about "labels" Two thousand years ago. if you were a slave or traitor. a mark would be branded on your skin. In Greek it is called stigma. that is, "stigmatization" This mark is very crude. With just one glance. everyone automatically stays 3 meters away from you. Now we no longer brand the skin. but switch to headlining. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "The deadly menace of the shut-in geek" The label is stamped onto the screen. and the effect is exactly the same. Sociology master Goffman. laid bare one thing. Stigma is not "something on your body" but a kind of "social relationship" Put simply. it is not that you are inherently problematic. but that society collectively decides. that some attribute of yours should be devalued. When we look at people we usually have two scripts. One is "virtual social identity" that is, we look at your appearance. and blindly guess in our heads. what kind of person you "should" be. The other is "actual social identity" that is, what kind of person. you "actually" are. When these two cannot connect. and happen to step on society's prejudice pain point. the label gets stuck on. Brother Goffman divides stigma into three major categories. which everyone can use to compare against today's news. The first category is bodily stigma. like disability or appearance differences. The media often portray them as. weaklings who can only be given charity. The second category is character stigma. like mental illness. unemployment or addiction. Complex social-institutional problems. are often simplified by the media into. "he just does not work hard himself" The third category is ethnic stigma. This is most often carried along by bloodline. The media often take a specific ethnic group. and directly equate it with specific criminals.

This labeling routine's. most powerful weapon is called "generalized flaw" The meaning is. that as long as one sees a black dot on you. the brain will automatically paint the whole thing black. When seeing "fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" what everyone thinks is not. "this 'one' person committed a crime" but they equate "all migrant workers" with "public order blind spots" This is actually collective anxiety grabbing a scapegoat. In communication studies it is called "moral panic" When everyone's days are hard. and they have no sense of security about the future. the media need only throw out a disadvantaged group. and the public's fury and unease. immediately have an outlet for venting. Discrimination is legalized all the way from the everyday. into stricter policies of exclusion. In the past the ancient Greek iron brand. could only scorch one person at a time. Modern media's steel seal. directly brands an entire group of people. directly making people too lazy to think. The previous segment talked about how media use labels. to demonize people. This segment let us look at a real example. In the past. Taiwan's flight attendants. once organized a strike. They sat in under the blazing sun. holding banners in their hands. protesting overwork scheduling. unreasonable wages. and working hours they could barely endure. At this point the media came. By rights their mission. is to convey the demands to the public. But this camera. was not aimed at the protest banners. but instead lingered on the calves. The next day's headline. "The most beautiful strike scenery" "Good-looking flight attendants sit in under the blazing sun" So in this strike. what did the audience finally see. Why is it that whenever women walk into the public sphere. the media's camera always "accidentally" tilts from their demands. onto their bodies. British scholar Gill. in "Gender and the Media" pointed out a very contradictory phenomenon. called "postfeminism" On one hand. the media shout "the rise of girl power" every day. But on the other hand. in the same channel. they sell body anxiety. Advertisements and reports that take women's figures. as a selling point. have never been in short supply. Gill points out. that the media play a very clever word game. In the past they treated women. as "objects to be looked at" Now they package women. as "subjects who actively want to become pretty" It sounds as if it is more progressive. but actually it is worse. because the power structure of "being stared at" has already been internalized into women's minds. Dieting. photo-editing. crazy fitness training. under the media's packaging. all become "pampering yourself" "being yourself" So a woman confidently showing off her figure. autonomously deciding how to dress up. is this not freedom. French thinker Foucault, Gill. their rebuttal is very sharp. The difference in it lies in. that the "list of autonomous options" you tick. exactly who wrote it. When the media take "appearance" as the unwritten rule of public exposure. where if you are not pretty no one pays you attention. you think you are freely choosing. but actually you are just obeying a set of. invisible rules. Looking back at the flight attendant strike (slip of the tongue). This was originally a labor-management. dispute concerning overwork scheduling. and high-pressure management. What it needed was society's.

rational dialogue about labor rights. As a result. the media did not film the data on the negotiation table. but specially filmed the profile of flight attendants wiping sweat. The headlines were uniformly. "The most beautiful strike scenery" A political protest against the system. was rewritten into one that lets everyone. feast their eyes on ice cream. a "visual consumption show" This camera that deliberately slides downward. is this label. machine's second gear. It does not directly tell you to shut up. It tells you to smile more sweetly. When your labor demands, in the news,. are swapped out for your waistline and your face. no matter how loud you shout. what more people pay attention to is instead. those enviable long legs. Now let us change direction. and aim the camera at an indigenous youth. This time the media did not tell him to shut up. but helped him change into a set of "costume" An Amis youth. wearing a modern shirt. at a press conference talking about land justice. the loss of traditional territory and the rupture of the mother tongue. these are all his contemporary situation. As a result the next day's news footage. showed indigenous costumes from who knows where. plus a big knife. The subtitle showed "Amis warrior" At that point who still remembers what demands he stated. Why is it that when mainstream society. is "praising" a minority group. they instead lose the right to speak. In postcolonial theory master. Said's "Orientalism" there is a concept called "othering" Put simply. the mainstream group with power. is not "describing" the disadvantaged. but "inventing" the disadvantaged. through the media painting the other side as. a backward. mysterious. exotic land. emphasizing that they and oneself. are "essentially different" This way mainstream society can. justifiably go manage him. even speak on his behalf. Cultural studies giant Hall. takes "stereotype" and dismantles it into four gears. The first is reduction. reducing a person's personality and background. down to only a few characteristics. Next is. essentialization. saying these few characteristics. are what this ethnic group. "innately carries in its DNA" Then. naturalization. taking artificially imposed categorization. and packaging it as "nature's original law" Finally fixation. making this flattened image jammed dead. forever not allowed to change. When these four gears turn to the end. they cut the world into two halves. On one side is "normal us" On the other side is. "abnormal them, full of peculiar exotic flavor" This machine, in Taiwan,. exactly how does it operate. The most typical. is the media's coverage of indigenous peoples. Actually each indigenous. people's institutions differ greatly. Some are matrilineal societies. some have strict class systems. and some have egalitarian elder councils. But in mainstream media. this depth and diversity. all disappear. Replacing them is a set of. Disney-cartoon-style words. "princess" "warrior" "chieftain" You may think. "princess" and "warrior" does this not sound like praise. what is wrong with this.

This is actually what Hall called. "naturalization"'s most vicious aspect. When the media use these "beautiful labels" to cover up all the real-world plight. the true problem can no longer be spoken. When the public becomes used to it. that indigenous people should, at the harvest festival,. sing and dance. innately passionate and humorous. what they, in reality,. face in employment discrimination. land rights being encroached upon. these get silenced by the singing and dancing. The Amis youth who was edited into festival footage. is not the TV station's error. but this label. machine's third gear. When mainstream society. insists on making you put on the "warrior" costume. before it is willing to give you the camera. you will find that this kind of. applause-carrying praise. is sometimes a gentler. and harder-to-remove hush money. So when the object this machine films. is not some ethnic group. but a poor person drifting on the streets. what kind of camera will it use. to make you believe. "his being poor is his own fault" You may have seen this kind of footage. a cramped little studio apartment. clothes scattered all over the floor. the kitchen full of grease. a single mother crouching in the corner. with a crying child beside her. The narration's tone is pressed very low. "She has no skill. the child's formula money. to this day still has no source" In just twenty seconds. at the moment you finish watching. a trace of sympathy may first rise in your heart. But perhaps there will be another voice. "Why does she not find a job. why does she not work a bit harder" This thinking process from "sympathy" turning toward "condemnation" is not because you are cold-blooded. but because this camera. chose a specific shot for you. American communication scholar Iyengar. did over a hundred experiments. and reached a conclusion. The way the media tell stories. is not only reporting news. but even more "assigning responsibility" He takes the media's narrative frame. and cuts it into two kinds of shots. One is the episodic frame. pushing the camera infinitely close. staring dead at some. "individual" or specific event. The other is the thematic frame. pulling the camera far away. to present, behind the event,. its "environment" and structural data. Brother Iyengar's experiment discovered. a major loophole in human nature. When the audience watches for a whole week straight. "telephoto lens" individual-case reporting. the brain will instinctively attribute poverty. crime or unemployment. all to. "the person himself being lazy. not working hard enough" Conversely. only when the audience sees. "wide-angle lens" thematic reporting. will they begin to reflect on the labor market. housing policy. and the social safety net, these institutional problems. The same social problem. with just a change of shot. the object of blame changes along with it. So why do today's media. so favor the telephoto lens. The reason is very realistic. The story is engaging. the cost is low. the emotional tension is strong. Filming an individual case's tears. takes only 20 seconds to hand in the job. But if one is to pull the camera far. and film clearly the labor market's structure. the media must spend 3 months. interviewing dozens of experts.

retrieving countless official documents. reports. In the torrent of instant news. the cost incentives of economy and time. overwhelm everything. Some people may speak up for the media. using individual-case stories to arouse sympathy. launch donation drives. making abstract issues have warmth. is this not a good thing. The key to the problem. has never been "having" individual cases. but that the media have "only" individual cases. When among 100 news items discussing poverty. 99 are all using the telephoto lens to push close. close-up on the person's misery. the audience's brain will be left with only. "this is all his personal problem" this standard answer. Political philosopher Fraser. criticizes this phenomenon very sharply. Mainstream media are most skilled at. taking institutional problems belonging to the public sphere. and "individualizing and familializing" them. The media package the problem as a family tragedy. quietly driving it off the negotiation table of debate. In sociology this. is the most typical "blaming the victim" Returning to that single mother. if today the media were willing to pull the camera far. switch to wide-angle, what would we see. We would see the closed-down factory. the rent risen to the ceiling. the severely insufficient public childcare. We would even see. the problem of the welfare-status review system. how, in reality, it takes countless. people on the edge of absolute poverty. and legally blocks them outside the door of social assistance. But these key institutional problems. the telephoto lens cannot fit in even one frame. So the distance of the camera. finally decides. society's conscience and resources. where they will finally be placed. Let us take a look. at when the media take all the gears. and aim them simultaneously at the same person. what will happen. On March 28, 2016. in Neihu a 4-year-old little girl. was killed by a stranger before her mother's eyes. From the incident to that evening. you turned on the TV. scrolled open your phone. and the headlines were uniformly. "mentally ill suspect" followed by "time bomb" "weirdo who calls himself Emperor Yao" "neighbors all thought he was strange" "loved playing violent video games" These words came overwhelmingly. In less than 24 hours. the puzzle in everyone's head. was pieced together. When "mentally ill suspect" these words fell down. did the fear in your heart. suddenly get settled down. Why, while everyone is still in shock,. are the media in such a hurry. to stuff the words "mental illness" into everyone's heads. Because this label. is actually society's collective. anxiety's fast painkiller. American scholar Wahl. in "Media Madness" points out. that the media always disproportionately. tie mental illness. violence. and villains together. And they dislike using medical terms. using in large quantities "lunatic" "psycho," this kind of slang. This is not only disrespectful. This is saving the audience the effort of "thinking" compressing complex medical and social problems. into an instantly understood terror symbol. But what is truly heartbreaking. are those details deleted by the headline. Like the killer, in 2010 and 2014,. had already shown behavior of attacking neighbors. and was also diagnosed with schizophrenia. That is to say. before the tragedy happened. our social safety net.

had already failed to catch him for a full 6 years. But this 6 years of "failure to catch" in that day's headlines. you cannot see a single word. The media do not want to explain. how the tragedy happened. It only wants to tell you "the killer is a monster" because exploring the causes behind it is too tiring. too complex. too sleep-depriving. So the media thoughtfully skip over it for you. Three years later, in July 2019,. Chiayi railway police officer Lee Cheng-han. was stabbed to death in the line of duty. The suspect likewise had schizophrenia. and likewise had long had medical records. likewise had discontinued medication. The words the media used. the rhythm. the footage. were almost exactly the same as three years before. The script did not change. only the actor was swapped. When the same play is staged repeatedly. this is no longer an individual event. but a stably operating structure. Since this medicine treats the symptom not the root. why does everyone still swallow it. Because every time a major random crime. the early morning the day after it erupts. while you eat breakfast. watching on the TV. a pundit angrily slam the table and shout. "this kind of lunatic should all be locked up" At this moment in your heart. a strange sense of relief will rise. because in that instant. between "the killer" and "you" a line is drawn. He is abnormal. and you are normal. This is not the solidness brought by truth. but a psychological defense line the media built for you. When extreme violence occurs in society. the answer we least want to hear. is instead that the killer. is actually an ordinary person. because this answer is too heavy. If we admit. that the killer is not some alien. but a person just like us. living under a high-pressure society. only that in isolation. failed to be caught by the system. with no way to retreat, he snapped. behind it actually represents. that crime is not walled off outside. but lurks in every overworked family. every laid-off middle-aged man. every living room before someone is caught. If we accept this truth. all Taiwan tonight, no one could sleep. So the media's machine starts at full speed. Hall's "division" gear begins to turn. classifying the suspect as "the abnormal other" confirming us as "safe normal people" Iyengar's "telephoto lens" is also pushed to the very front. The camera aims at that abnormal brain. while the world outside the wide-angle lens. the overworked labor environment. the safety net full of holes. the long-insufficient mental-health resources. are all locked into darkness. In Taiwanese society every time after a case. our real reaction. is the best evidence. On social media it is forever. "lock up the lunatics" "compulsory treatment cannot be delayed" "mental illness equals a death-exemption gold medal" "death penalty the only option" The core of these slogans. is all not asking why. they went long uncaught. but "how to cut them out" Communication scholar Gerbner. puts it very heavily. This kind of attribution only helps us. escape collective responsibility. When you shout to lock them up. sentence them to death. your anxiety is relieved. but the core that could truly solve the problem. is also let go with your own hands. But this wall is not un-topplable. In that year's incident.

the person most entitled to be angry. Little Light Bulb's mother, Wang Wan-yu,. instead refused the media's. handed-over painkiller. She did not shout along. to lock up all the lunatics. but calmly asked society. to mend the holes in the safety net. She said in court. that compared to the killer being executed. she cared more about. "the next time I take my child out to the street. not needing to be on edge with worry anymore" Although some people. would, because of ideology. or differences in political stance. use the tragedy that happened to her. to make some jokes. but after years of advocacy. the "Mental Health Act" in 2022. completed a large-scale revision. This proves one thing. The wall the media blocked up for you. everyone can push open with their own hands. But the premise is. that we are willing to hear the crying outside the wall. rather than being in a hurry to swallow the painkiller. When the majority of people. still choose to swallow the painkiller. pretending the world is very safe. the ones truly silently bearing the pain. exactly who are they. Actually it is every one of us. When you lie on the sofa scrolling your phone. a sensational crime headline. a simplified poverty close-up. an indigenous youth crowned with "princess" or "warrior" At this point please stop and ask yourself. while the media label things for us. how should you press the pause button. As a modern citizen. what weapons do we have left to resist it. A-Niu feels that every one of us. has two major self-defense moves. "decoding" and "resistance" "Decoding" is learning. to see through the magic behind the news. Next time you see the news. try to dismantle in your heart. whether its camera is pushing infinitely close. or slowly pulling far. Is it focusing on personal grudges. or presenting the social context. How many times does it let some identity label. get repeatedly bombarded. On whom does it finally. blame the responsibility. These four questions. are your magnifying glass for dismantling media labels. "Resistance" is refusing to be an accomplice. When you scroll to a. report attributing poverty to "not working hard" you can choose not to like it. not to forward it. When you see a labor protest. simplified into "the most beautiful strike scenery" you can proactively refuse to watch. and turn to find independent media that earnestly report. When you see "mentally ill suspect" again beginning to occupy all the pages. you can choose to press, in the comment section,. whether that social safety net that failed to catch him. over the past few years has been mended or not. A-Niu finally leaves a question. I want to hear everyone's views. When mainstream media continue to use. "princess" "warrior" or "innately optimistic and loves to drink," these words. to consume indigenous peoples. if you hold the microphone of self-media. how would you return the right to speak to them. letting them use their own words. to tell their own contemporary stories. We welcome everyone to share your views. Our channel has always been. committed to the idea of "rebuilding the republic" hoping through civic. education and historical awareness. to awaken everyone's. appreciation for democratic values. If you enjoyed this episode. do not forget to like. subscribe. and share it with more people. You are also welcome to join our membership.

So we will see you next time. Bye Bye.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iLjAjfgm9aY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析媒體如何透過「貼標籤」與簡化機制，將社會焦慮轉嫁至弱勢族群並引發對立。
  • 結合高夫曼、吉爾、傅柯、薩伊德與霍爾等多位大師的社會學與傳播理論，提供扎實的批判性思考架構。
  • 透過台灣空服員罷工與原住民爭取權益等真實案例，揭露主流媒體如何以「視覺消費」與「刻板印象」抹煞抗爭者的真實話語權。

摘要

媒體標籤與社會污名化機制

作者指出，現代媒體為迎合大眾有限的注意力，慣用「化繁為簡」的標題將特定群體與社會問題劃上等號。這種簡化對主流群體而言是便捷摘要，對邊緣弱勢族群卻是長期的制度化傷害。作者引用社會學家高夫曼（Erving Goffman）的理論，說明污名（Stigma）並非個人內在缺陷，而是一種社會關係，源自於大眾預期的「虛擬社會身分」與「真實社會身分」產生落差。媒體透過身體污名、性格污名與族群污名，利用「全面性缺陷」的心理機制將少數個案放大為群體標籤，藉由製造道德恐慌（Moral Panic）將邊緣族群塑造成社會焦慮的代罪羔羊。

後女性主義與抗爭訴求的視覺消費化

作者以台灣空服員罷工為例，揭示媒體如何透過鏡頭轉移焦點來消解嚴肅議題。原本抗議過勞排班與爭取勞動權益的集體行動，在媒體鏡頭下卻聚焦於女性外貌與身材，被包裝成「最美罷工風景」。作者引述學者吉爾（Rosalind Gill）的後女性主義觀點以及傅柯（Michel Foucault）的權力理論，指出媒體常將女性包裝為「自主追求美麗的主體」，實質上是將被凝視的權力結構內化為審美規訓。當勞動訴求被置換為長腿與顏值，一場體制抗爭便被徹底降格為供大眾娛樂的視覺消費秀。

他者化與刻板印象的四重齒輪

作者進一步探討原住民族群在媒體報導中的失語困境。當原住民青年身著現代服裝爭取土地正義與母語權益時，媒體往往將其套上傳統服飾並冠上「勇士」稱號，抹煞其當代處境。作者結合薩伊德（Edward Said）的他者化（Othering）概念與霍爾（Stuart Hall）的刻板印象理論，拆解媒體運作的四重齒輪：化約（Reduction）、本質化（Essentialization）、自然化（Naturalization）與固著（Fixation）。主流媒體將多元豐富的文化深度簡化為迪士尼式的「公主」與「勇士」，用看似讚美的標籤掩飾真實壓迫，使大眾忽視原住民族群在現實社會中所面臨的真正困境。

================================================

Hello! Everyone! This is A-Niu. Today let us talk about media "labeling" You may ask, is this important. Of course it is important. because this label. very easily causes social antagonism. When you watch the news. you must have seen similar headlines. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "Most beautiful striking flight attendant sits in under the blazing sun" "Young people are poor only because they do not work hard" Every news headline. is like a simple equation. Some person. equals some kind of social problem. You scroll your phone very fast. almost never stopping to think. Without your knowing it. inside your head. labels have already been stuck on one after another. After you turn off your phone. have these labels disappeared. But have you ever thought. why they headline it this way. Because every day too many things happen in the world. and our brain's attention is too weak. So the media choose. to "simplify the complex" But the problem is this simplifying of the complex. for the mainstream group. is a thoughtful summary cheat sheet. but for marginal disadvantaged groups. it is a slow torture. A corporate CEO. if simplified or misunderstood by the news. still has a huge PR. and lawyer team to help him clarify. But a migrant worker. a mental illness patient. when he is simplified into a headline by the news. that label often follows him for a lifetime. What is more frightening. is that once a label has been stuck on long enough. society becomes used to it as normal. This is what in academia is called. "institutionalization" and "normalization" So today let us talk about "labels" Two thousand years ago. if you were a slave or traitor. a mark would be branded on your skin. In Greek it is called stigma. that is, "stigmatization" This mark is very crude. With just one glance. everyone automatically stays 3 meters away from you. Now we no longer brand the skin. but switch to headlining. "Fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" "The deadly menace of the shut-in geek" The label is stamped onto the screen. and the effect is exactly the same. Sociology master Goffman. laid bare one thing. Stigma is not "something on your body" but a kind of "social relationship" Put simply. it is not that you are inherently problematic. but that society collectively decides. that some attribute of yours should be devalued. When we look at people we usually have two scripts. One is "virtual social identity" that is, we look at your appearance. and blindly guess in our heads. what kind of person you "should" be. The other is "actual social identity" that is, what kind of person. you "actually" are. When these two cannot connect. and happen to step on society's prejudice pain point. the label gets stuck on. Brother Goffman divides stigma into three major categories. which everyone can use to compare against today's news. The first category is bodily stigma. like disability or appearance differences. The media often portray them as. weaklings who can only be given charity. The second category is character stigma. like mental illness. unemployment or addiction. Complex social-institutional problems. are often simplified by the media into. "he just does not work hard himself" The third category is ethnic stigma. This is most often carried along by bloodline. The media often take a specific ethnic group. and directly equate it with specific criminals.

This labeling routine's. most powerful weapon is called "generalized flaw" The meaning is. that as long as one sees a black dot on you. the brain will automatically paint the whole thing black. When seeing "fugitive migrant worker commits crime again" what everyone thinks is not. "this 'one' person committed a crime" but they equate "all migrant workers" with "public order blind spots" This is actually collective anxiety grabbing a scapegoat. In communication studies it is called "moral panic" When everyone's days are hard. and they have no sense of security about the future. the media need only throw out a disadvantaged group. and the public's fury and unease. immediately have an outlet for venting. Discrimination is legalized all the way from the everyday. into stricter policies of exclusion. In the past the ancient Greek iron brand. could only scorch one person at a time. Modern media's steel seal. directly brands an entire group of people. directly making people too lazy to think. The previous segment talked about how media use labels. to demonize people. This segment let us look at a real example. In the past. Taiwan's flight attendants. once organized a strike. They sat in under the blazing sun. holding banners in their hands. protesting overwork scheduling. unreasonable wages. and working hours they could barely endure. At this point the media came. By rights their mission. is to convey the demands to the public. But this camera. was not aimed at the protest banners. but instead lingered on the calves. The next day's headline. "The most beautiful strike scenery" "Good-looking flight attendants sit in under the blazing sun" So in this strike. what did the audience finally see. Why is it that whenever women walk into the public sphere. the media's camera always "accidentally" tilts from their demands. onto their bodies. British scholar Gill. in "Gender and the Media" pointed out a very contradictory phenomenon. called "postfeminism" On one hand. the media shout "the rise of girl power" every day. But on the other hand. in the same channel. they sell body anxiety. Advertisements and reports that take women's figures. as a selling point. have never been in short supply. Gill points out. that the media play a very clever word game. In the past they treated women. as "objects to be looked at" Now they package women. as "subjects who actively want to become pretty" It sounds as if it is more progressive. but actually it is worse. because the power structure of "being stared at" has already been internalized into women's minds. Dieting. photo-editing. crazy fitness training. under the media's packaging. all become "pampering yourself" "being yourself" So a woman confidently showing off her figure. autonomously deciding how to dress up. is this not freedom. French thinker Foucault, Gill. their rebuttal is very sharp. The difference in it lies in. that the "list of autonomous options" you tick. exactly who wrote it. When the media take "appearance" as the unwritten rule of public exposure. where if you are not pretty no one pays you attention. you think you are freely choosing. but actually you are just obeying a set of. invisible rules. Looking back at the flight attendant strike (slip of the tongue). This was originally a labor-management. dispute concerning overwork scheduling. and high-pressure management. What it needed was society's.

rational dialogue about labor rights. As a result. the media did not film the data on the negotiation table. but specially filmed the profile of flight attendants wiping sweat. The headlines were uniformly. "The most beautiful strike scenery" A political protest against the system. was rewritten into one that lets everyone. feast their eyes on ice cream. a "visual consumption show" This camera that deliberately slides downward. is this label. machine's second gear. It does not directly tell you to shut up. It tells you to smile more sweetly. When your labor demands, in the news,. are swapped out for your waistline and your face. no matter how loud you shout. what more people pay attention to is instead. those enviable long legs. Now let us change direction. and aim the camera at an indigenous youth. This time the media did not tell him to shut up. but helped him change into a set of "costume" An Amis youth. wearing a modern shirt. at a press conference talking about land justice. the loss of traditional territory and the rupture of the mother tongue. these are all his contemporary situation. As a result the next day's news footage. showed indigenous costumes from who knows where. plus a big knife. The subtitle showed "Amis warrior" At that point who still remembers what demands he stated. Why is it that when mainstream society. is "praising" a minority group. they instead lose the right to speak. In postcolonial theory master. Said's "Orientalism" there is a concept called "othering" Put simply. the mainstream group with power. is not "describing" the disadvantaged. but "inventing" the disadvantaged. through the media painting the other side as. a backward. mysterious. exotic land. emphasizing that they and oneself. are "essentially different" This way mainstream society can. justifiably go manage him. even speak on his behalf. Cultural studies giant Hall. takes "stereotype" and dismantles it into four gears. The first is reduction. reducing a person's personality and background. down to only a few characteristics. Next is. essentialization. saying these few characteristics. are what this ethnic group. "innately carries in its DNA" Then. naturalization. taking artificially imposed categorization. and packaging it as "nature's original law" Finally fixation. making this flattened image jammed dead. forever not allowed to change. When these four gears turn to the end. they cut the world into two halves. On one side is "normal us" On the other side is. "abnormal them, full of peculiar exotic flavor" This machine, in Taiwan,. exactly how does it operate. The most typical. is the media's coverage of indigenous peoples. Actually each indigenous. people's institutions differ greatly. Some are matrilineal societies. some have strict class systems. and some have egalitarian elder councils. But in mainstream media. this depth and diversity. all disappear. Replacing them is a set of. Disney-cartoon-style words. "princess" "warrior" "chieftain" You may think. "princess" and "warrior" does this not sound like praise. what is wrong with this.

This is actually what Hall called. "naturalization"'s most vicious aspect. When the media use these "beautiful labels" to cover up all the real-world plight. the true problem can no longer be spoken. When the public becomes used to it. that indigenous people should, at the harvest festival,. sing and dance. innately passionate and humorous. what they, in reality,. face in employment discrimination. land rights being encroached upon. these get silenced by the singing and dancing. The Amis youth who was edited into festival footage. is not the TV station's error. but this label. machine's third gear. When mainstream society. insists on making you put on the "warrior" costume. before it is willing to give you the camera. you will find that this kind of. applause-carrying praise. is sometimes a gentler. and harder-to-remove hush money. So when the object this machine films. is not some ethnic group. but a poor person drifting on the streets. what kind of camera will it use. to make you believe. "his being poor is his own fault" You may have seen this kind of footage. a cramped little studio apartment. clothes scattered all over the floor. the kitchen full of grease. a single mother crouching in the corner. with a crying child beside her. The narration's tone is pressed very low. "She has no skill. the child's formula money. to this day still has no source" In just twenty seconds. at the moment you finish watching. a trace of sympathy may first rise in your heart. But perhaps there will be another voice. "Why does she not find a job. why does she not work a bit harder" This thinking process from "sympathy" turning toward "condemnation" is not because you are cold-blooded. but because this camera. chose a specific shot for you.
